create_barcode.description: Turn an order number, SKU, tracking code or any other text into a barcode image, in any of 33 common types: Code 128, Code 39, GS1-128, ITF-14, Data Matrix, PDF417, Aztec, postal barcodes and more. The image is saved so later steps can print, attach or upload it. No account or API key required.
create_barcode.name: create_barcode

parameters.description: What the barcode should hold. Each type accepts different characters: Code 128 takes any plain text, retail and postal types take their own number formats, and GS1 types take data written like (01)09521234543213(10)ABC123.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The kind of barcode to draw. Code 128 suits almost anything; pick another when a scanner, retailer or carrier asks for it.
parameters.name: barcode_type

options.label: QR code, links and text for phones
UPC-A, retail products in the US and Canada
Data Matrix, small parts and healthcare labels
Code 39, badges and inventory (capitals and digits)
PDF417, ID cards and boarding passes
Aztec code, tickets and transport passes
GS1 Data Matrix, healthcare and traceability
GS1 Digital Link QR code, QR codes on retail products
GS1 DataBar Expanded, weighed goods and coupons
USPS Intelligent Mail, US letters and flats
Micro QR code, very small labels (short text)

parameters.description: Print the barcode's contents in plain text under the bars, so a person can read it too. 2D codes such as QR and Data Matrix never show it.
parameters.name: show_text

parameters.description: How wide the thinnest bar is, in pixels, between 1 and 10. Everything else grows with it: 3 suits screens and labels, 5 or more a large print.
parameters.name: size

parameters.description: Optional. How tall the bars are, in millimetres at full size, between 5 and 100. Leave blank for the standard height. 2D codes, postal barcodes and GS1 DataBar keep their standard shape whatever this says.
parameters.name: height_mm

parameters.description: Which way round the barcode is drawn, for labels that run sideways.
parameters.name: rotation

options.label: Turned right, a quarter turn clockwise
Turned left, a quarter turn anticlockwise

parameters.description: The colour of the bars and text, as a hex colour. It has to be clearly darker than the background or scanners will not read it.
parameters.name: foreground_color

parameters.description: The colour behind the code, as a hex colour. Keep it light so the code stands out.
parameters.name: background_color

parameters.description: Blank space around the barcode, counted in thinnest-bar widths. 10 is what scanners expect; use 0 if your label design already leaves space around it.
parameters.name: border

parameters.description: Optional. The name to save the image under. Named after what the code holds by default, e.g. lodol-1234-barcode.png.
parameters.name: filename

barcode_type.description: The kind of code that was made, for example Code 128.

create_product_barcode.description: Make the retail barcode for a product number: EAN-13, UPC-A, EAN-8, UPC-E or a book's ISBN. Enter the number with or without its check digit; a missing one is worked out, and a wrong one is caught before anything is printed. No account or API key required.
create_product_barcode.name: create_product_barcode

parameters.description: The number printed under the barcode, with or without its last (check) digit. Spaces and hyphens are ignored. Write an ISBN with its hyphens to have it printed above the barcode, as on a book.

parameters.description: Which numbering the product uses. EAN-13 is the standard almost everywhere; UPC-A is used in the US and Canada.

create_qr_code.description: Turn a link or any other text into a QR code image, ready to email, print or drop into a document. Accented letters, other alphabets and emoji all work. The image is saved so later steps can attach or upload it. No account or API key required.
create_qr_code.name: create_qr_code

parameters.description: What the code should hold. A web address opens when scanned; anything else is shown as text.

examples.label: A phone number that dials when scanned

parameters.name: content

parameters.description: How much of the code can be scratched, smudged or covered and still scan. Stronger levels make the pattern denser, so step up only for things that get handled.
parameters.name: error_correction

options.label: Strongest, for signs and worn surfaces

parameters.description: How big the code is drawn, between 1 and 10. Each step adds 2 pixels to every square: 4 makes a short link about 260 pixels across, and longer text makes a bigger code.
parameters.name: size

parameters.description: The colour of the code itself, as a hex colour. It has to be clearly darker than the background or scanners will not read it.
parameters.name: foreground_color

parameters.description: The colour behind the code, as a hex colour. Keep it light so the code stands out.
parameters.name: background_color

parameters.description: Blank space around the code, counted in code squares. 4 is the standard and scans most reliably; use 0 if your design already leaves space around it.
parameters.name: border

parameters.description: Optional. The name to save the image under. qr-code.png by default.
parameters.name: filename

description: Make barcodes and QR codes with bwip-js, the open-source barcode library. Turn order numbers, SKUs and tracking codes into Code 128, GS1-128, ITF-14, Data Matrix, PDF417, Aztec, postal barcodes and two dozen more; make QR codes that hold links or any text; and make retail EAN, UPC and ISBN barcodes with the check digit worked out and checked for you. Choose the size, colours and rotation, and get a PNG ready to print, email or upload. No account or API key required.
